Your hiccups might be a leftover from ancestors with gills 🐸

In a hiccup your diaphragm suddenly yanks air in and your vocal cords snap shut. Tadpoles do almost the same move to push water over their gills: they suck in hard and shut the glottis so water can't flood their lungs. Scientists proposed the link in 2003. It's a hypothesis, not proven, but babies even hiccup in the womb before they start practicing breathing.

Hiccups usually stop within minutes. See a doctor if they last more than 48 hours.

Sources: BioEssays (Straus et al. 2003), Scientific American, Mayo Clinic, NHS, Cleveland Clinic.
